question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

The apple of one’s eye
solution:
The correct answer is** Option 2)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"The apple of one's eye"** means someone who is cherished above all others; someone who is very dear. (किसी की आँखों का तारा)

 
 
• **Example:** Her youngest son is the **apple of her eye.**
 
 
 
• **Very dear** refers to someone or something that is loved or valued greatly. (बहुत प्यारा)
 
 
• **Example:** She is **very dear **to her grandparents.
 
 

Therefore, the correct meaning of the given idiom is **'Very dear.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Very cheerful** (बहुत खुश): Feeling or showing happiness.

 
 
• **Example:** She always has a **very cheerful **disposition.
 
 
 
• **Very nice** (बहुत अच्छा): Pleasant, agreeable, or satisfactory.
 
 
• **Example:** The weather today is** very nice** for a picnic.
 
 
 
• **Very pleasing** (बहुत सुखद): Giving pleasure or satisfaction.
 
 
• **Example:** The music was **very pleasing **to the ears.
